name: Pula
title: Ship Thickness Measurement in Pula | UTM and Hull Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Pula for cruise ships, ferries, tankers and cargo vessels: hull, tank and deck readings for surveys and condition checks.
h1: Pula Ship Gauging: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement in Pula Bay
intro: Pula sits at the southern tip of the Istrian peninsula, in a deep natural bay that has served ships since Roman times. Cruise ships, ferries, bulk and general cargo vessels, and tankers calling for the nearby oil terminal all use its berths and anchorages. Atlantis NDT sends ultrasonic gauging technicians from India to the ship, wherever in the bay it lies, for survey preparation, owner condition checks and pre-purchase work.

highlights.p: Pula Bay is sheltered from open-sea swell, so ships at anchor or alongside are steady enough for careful readings on decks, hatch covers and tank tops, and launches can reach vessels waiting in the bay.
Pula has long been a shipbuilding town, but yard capacity there has changed over the years. We treat any dockings as something to confirm with the owner and the ship's agent rather than assume.

highlights.h: Cruise and ferry calls in season
highlights.p: Summer brings cruise and ferry traffic to the city quays, with short call-day windows suited to technical spaces and scrubber piping, while cargo and tanker calls run throughout the year.

port.h: Pula Bay: geography, approach and berths
p: Pula lies on the western side of the Istrian peninsula, where a long, protected bay opens to the northern Adriatic through a relatively narrow entrance. That geography has made it a natural harbour for centuries, and the port authority today manages a number of separate working areas around the bay rather than one single quay front. Passenger and cruise ships use the quays close to the old town and its Roman amphitheatre, while cargo berths and industrial quays lie further around the shore. Pilotage is compulsory for larger ships, and the entrance channel and the inner bay are well marked, so approach and departure follow a routine that agents and pilots know thoroughly.

Traffic is varied rather than heavy. In summer, cruise ships and excursion vessels bring most of the visible activity to the waterfront, alongside regional ferry services to the nearby islands and the Brijuni archipelago. Throughout the year, general cargo, timber and bulk carriers call at the commercial berths, and small product tankers deliver fuel for the regional market. Smaller craft such as tugs, pilot boats, fishing vessels and workboats are based in the bay and need periodic condition checks of their own. This mixture means a gauging job in Pula might be a short check on a visiting ship or a longer programme on a vessel laid up in the bay.

The bay offers several anchorage areas, and ships waiting for a berth, for orders or for a change of crew often lie there for a day or more. Because the water is sheltered, launches can reach a ship at anchor in most conditions; the main limiting factors are winter bora wind events from the north-east, which can interrupt boat transfers for a day, and the ship's own cargo or ballast operations. Tidal range is small by northern European standards, so berthing depth and freeboard change little during a shift, which simplifies the access arrangements for staging on decks and hold coamings. Owners looking for a quiet place to lay a ship up between charters sometimes choose the bay for exactly this reason.

facilities.h: Where gauging can be carried out in and around Pula
p: The practical question in Pula is not whether a ship can be reached but what kind of work suits each location. Pula has a long shipbuilding history, and yard facilities on the bay have changed in recent years. We therefore do not assume a drydock slot here: where an owner plans a docking, the yard, dock dimensions and availability are confirmed with the ship's agent and the superintendent before we plan the programme, and ships needing a large dock are often directed to Rijeka or an Italian yard instead.

For work that does not need a dock, the commercial quays and the bay itself offer realistic options. Ships alongside during a cargo stop can be gauged on deck, hatch covers, coamings and any holds the crew can make safe once cargo is out. Ships at anchor can be reached by launch for pre-purchase, on-hire or off-hire condition work and for pre-docking steel estimates. Cruise ships and ferries at the city quays offer shorter windows, mainly for technical spaces, scrubber piping and ballast tanks that the ship's engineers can certify for entry. The agent arranges port access and any launch transfers.

City passenger quays — scrubber discharge piping, ballast tanks and technical spaces on cruise ships during a call day
Island ferry berths — vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks on regional ferries during winter lay-up
Pula Bay anchorages — launch access for pre-purchase, on-hire and pre-docking gauging on ships waiting in the bay
Lay-up areas in the bay — longer condition programmes on vessels idle between charters
Shipyard facilities on the bay — docking work only after availability is confirmed with the owner and the agent

context.h: Port state control, regulation and the Istrian trade
p: Foreign ships calling at Pula are subject to port state control under the Paris MoU, carried out by Croatian officers working under the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure and its harbour master's authorities along the coast. Because the northern Adriatic is busy, a ship arriving at Pula may already have been inspected at an Italian or Slovenian port, and recent deficiency records influence how closely she is targeted. Structural findings, especially corroded tank boundaries or weak hatch coamings, can lead to detention, so owners with older ships sometimes commission gauging before arrival to find out what the inspector might find.

EU environmental rules also shape inspection work here. Larger ships calling at an EU port need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on board under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, and ships above the size thresholds report emissions under EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime. Older tonnage is increasingly evaluated against those obligations at the same time as its steel condition, so gauging results feed directly into decisions about repair, sale or recycling. Istria's economy rests heavily on tourism, timber and construction materials, so the cargo ships we see are typically small to mid-sized, often with decades of service behind them.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Pula
jobs.p: Pula jobs tend to be targeted rather than large. A cargo ship discharging timber or aggregates might need hatch covers and tank tops gauged during the stop; a cruise or ferry operator might want ballast tanks and scrubber piping checked in a call window; an owner considering a purchase might want the whole hull assessed at anchor. We agree scope with the superintendent before the team travels, then report on the class formats where the owner needs them.
list: Pre-purchase gauging of a coaster at anchor in Pula Bay: deck, hatch covers, coamings, ballast tanks and accessible hold structure
Hatch cover and coaming readings on a timber carrier after discharge at a commercial quay, preparing for an intermediate survey
Scrubber discharge piping and shell around the overboard outlet on a cruise ship during a short call, taken with the system shut down
Winter lay-up gauging on a regional ferry: vehicle deck, ramp, void spaces and ballast tanks, planned ahead of its docking elsewhere
Steel estimate for a tug or workboat based in the bay, giving the owner measured values before committing to repair

logistics: Pula Airport serves seasonal European routes, with Trieste, Zagreb and Ljubljana offering wider connections within road distance of Istria. The ship's agent arranges port access passes for the quays and books launches for ships at anchor. Croatia is within Schengen, so technicians travelling from India need a Schengen visa, and the timing of the visa decides when a team can join the ship. Where a call is short, the dates should be passed to us as early as the schedule allows.

faqs.q: Can a ship be gauged at anchor in Pula Bay?
faqs.a: Yes. Launches can usually reach ships in the bay because the water is sheltered, and gauging at anchor suits pre-purchase, on-hire and pre-docking work. Tanks need to be gas-free and certified for entry by the ship, and a bora wind event can pause launch transfers for a day, so a spare day in the plan is sensible.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Pula for a docking survey?
faqs.a: Pula has a shipbuilding history, but we do not promise dock availability. The yard situation should be confirmed with the owner and the ship's agent at the planning stage. If no suitable dock is free, many owners choose Rijeka, an Italian yard or another Adriatic port, and we gauge at the pre-docking stage in Pula Bay.

faqs.q: Can cruise ships be gauged during a normal call?
faqs.a: Partly. A call day gives access to technical spaces, scrubber piping and ballast tanks the engineers have made safe, but not to a full hull programme. Full coverage needs a dock or a longer lay-up, so we plan call-day work around the ship's critical items and leave the bottom shell for a docking.

faqs.q: Do you work on small craft based in Pula?
faqs.a: Yes. Tugs, pilot vessels, fishing boats and workboats can be gauged alongside, and owners often use the readings to decide how much steel to renew. We adjust probe selection and measurement spacing to the plate thickness and the access available.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover Pula and other Croatian ports?
faqs.a: Often. A Schengen visa covers all of Croatia, and Rijeka and the Istrian coast are reachable by road. If an owner has ships in more than one Adriatic port, we can sequence the work in one mobilisation and issue a separate report for each vessel.
